_source: Built 2026-10-23 from the real site: the 6 live pages in real-inventory.json plus the 14 products in the live catalog-data.js. Replaces the sitemap-era clusters, now in data/retired/.
_owner_rule: canonical_owner is null until the Owner sets it. A null owner makes the cluster a HOLD for any new package. Setting one is an Owner decision, never a code change.
_why_all_owners_are_null: The Owner decided on 2026-10-23 that products get their own URLs. That settles the product level. It does NOT settle which page owns a generic head term like 'เครื่องสแกนบาร์โค้ด': the candidates are the catalogue /products.html, a per-category page that does not exist yet, or the filtered view /products.html?category=scanners. Until that is decided, writing a package against a head term risks building the page that then has to be thrown away — which is exactly what this gate exists to prevent.

decisions_needed.question: Do category pages exist as their own URLs, or is the filtered catalogue (/products.html?category=X) the canonical home for each category head term?
decisions_needed.note: A query-parameter view is a weak canonical owner: it is one page serving six different head terms. Real category pages are stronger but are six more pages to write and evidence.

decisions_needed.question: Three ribbon products (wax, wax-resin, resin) will all target the same intent, 'ริบบอน / thermal transfer ribbon'. Do they get three pages with one owning the head term, or one page covering the choice between them?
decisions_needed.note: This is the sharpest cannibalisation risk on the site and it does not exist yet — the pages are not built. Deciding now costs nothing; deciding after costs three pages.

decisions_needed.question: Where does the approved about-ACS copy live, now that /why-acs returns 404?
decisions_needed.note: Content and evidence stand (CR-06, CR-10 closed). Only the target URL was wrong. The homepage is currently the only company surface.
